text:
hannah_support: customer reports intermittent 401s and a billing spike, says they can't find any request id in their UI. pasted their minimal header screenshot (image omitted) — header shows Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, but no x-request-id. need a concise set of steps to get us a reproducible request id and a curl we can run. they’re non-technical on the first pass, but can follow step-by-step.

raj_support: quick checklist to send to customer (non-technical): 1) open the page that errors, 2) open developer console (F12 / right click -> Inspect), 3) go to Network tab, 4) repro the error, 5) click the failing request and copy the request headers + response status screenshot. ask them to attach a screenshot and the time they repro'd (UTC). keep it short. :thumbsup:

emma_eng: adding the engineer-friendly details / curl template and debug-token flow. the most important things we need: a raw request header snapshot (including any x-req-* headers), the exact timestamp (±30s), and, if possible, a short curl that reproduces the call. if auth is 401, include the token prefix (redact token body) and the SDK + version.

emma_eng: curl template customers can use to reproduce (ask them to run from a dev machine):
```
# replace <URL> and <API_KEY_MASKED> before running
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY_MASKED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Source: customer-ui" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

emma_eng: if they can run the curl and still hit 401, ask them to add the debug header we use so the platform will emit a debug-token for the session: add `-H "X-Redwood-Debug: capture"` and then report the debug token printed in the response headers (we return `x-debug-token: <token>`). sample:
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY_MASKED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Debug: capture" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
# look for: < HTTP/1.1 401 ...
# and a response header: x-debug-token: abc123def456
```

hannah_support: nice, can you also add quick iOS / Android hints? some customers can’t run curl.

emma_eng: sure — iOS (UIKit/WebView) from a non-dev user: Settings -> Developer -> Safari -> Web Inspector (or ask them to remote screen share). For React Native / native SDKs ask them to: 1) enable verbose network logging for the SDK (we document toggles in console), 2) reproduce, 3) send a screenshot of the SDK logs showing the request start/response status and any x-debug-token in headers.

emma_eng: short copy they can paste to the customer (non-technical):
"Hi — sorry about the 401. Can you please: (1) reproduce the issue and take a screenshot of the browser/devtools Network tab showing the failed request, (2) note the exact time (UTC) the failure happened, and (3) if possible, run this curl and paste the output (replace the token with the masked value we sent): 

(curl command)

If you see a response header called x-debug-token, please paste that value here. If you can’t run curl, a screenshot of the failing Network request + time is enough to start."

raj_support: small tip — ask them to include the request method + path (POST /v1/generate) and any query params. that helps us find traces quickly. also ask whether they’re on Redwood hosted or Dedicated (customer said hosted earlier).

hannah_support: copying the final one-liner for the ticket body and escalation: "Please ask customer for: (A) screenshot of the failing request from Network tab, (B) exact UTC timestamp, (C) curl output with X-Redwood-Debug: capture if they can run it, (D) SDK + version if used."

ops-bot: debug-token created for manual capture — token=dbg-7f3e9 (this is a simulated token; ask customer to run curl with X-Redwood-Debug: capture to get their session-specific token).

emma_eng: once we have a debug token or screenshot+time, we can map to a trace id and share server-side spans. if the customer is seeing billing mismatch also include the transaction id from their billing UI (if they have one) — we correlate by timestamp and trace.

hannah_support: will send to customer now. tagging @raj_support to handle follow-ups if they share the screenshot only.

raj_support: got it, will monitor. if they paste only a token I'll pull the trace and attach a short audit log excerpt for billing team.

hannah_support: thanks team — saving this as a short template for the next rep. :saved:
